sentences.text: The accused in C.C.No.279 of 2001 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class -1, Mananthavady filed this Revision Petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Section 16(1A) (i) read with Section 7(i) and Section 2(ia)(a) & (j) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rule 5, Appendix B. A.18.06.09 and Rule 29 of PFA Rules.

entities.text: Section 16(1A) (i) read with Section 7(i) and Section 2(ia)(a) & (j)
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text:
2. Heard.
3.

The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 16.11.2000 at about 11.00 a.m., PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased 750 gm. of toor dal from the shop of the second accused.
First accused was the salesman of the said shop.
After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst.

The Public Analyst filed Ext. P13 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for toor dal under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1956 and therefore, the same was adulterated.
Thereafter, on the request of the revision petitioners, another sample was sent for the examination to the Central Food Laboratory.
Ext.C1 certificate of the Central Food Laboratory would also show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for toor dal and therefore, it was adulterated.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts. P1 to P25 and C1 were marked for the prosecution.
DW1 to DW3 were examined and Exts.D1 to D4 series were marked for the revision petitioners.

5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. C1 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated.
The learned counsel for the revision petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A)
(ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act.

Therefore, Ext.C1 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in K.C.Sharafudheen vs The Food Inspector on 12 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164582765/
2

entities.text: K.C.Sharafudheen vs The Food Inspector on 12 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Pepsico India Holdings (supra).

It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra)
that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal.

In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.

Even otherwise, in view of the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra), the conviction in this case cannot be sustained as no laboratory was notified and no validated method of analysis was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

In the result, this Revision Petition stands allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sec 16(1A) (i) read with Sections 7(i) and 2(ia)(a) and (j) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rule 5, Appendix B. A.18.06.09 and Rule 29 of PFA Rules and the revision petitioners are acquitted for the said offence.
